newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela mulls buybacks to restructure debt.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela mulls buybacks to restructure debt.

text.p: The Venezuelan government is considering options, including debt buybacks, to restructure its roughly $25 billion in foreign debt, a top government official said Wednesday.
"The mechanism includes the buyback and repayment of public debt," Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Poletto told a conference of industrialists.
Heavy debt expiries over the next three years make a restructuring plan essential, said the head of the FIV, which is working with the Central Bank and Finance Ministry on the debt project.
"By restructuring the debt, we will be creating a better situation for the country's development," Poletto said.
According to Finance Ministry figures, Venezuela's public foreign debt stood at $24.726 billion at the end of 1996, down from $26.901 billion at the end of 1995.
The government made foreign debt principal payments of $2.415 billion and interest payments of $1.748 billion last year, the figures showed.
